subject.title: [Bug]: ACP concurrent session spawns — first agent fails to launch CC process

question: Should OpenClaw preserve distinct ACP child-session parallelism and require a narrow launch-readiness fix, or intentionally gate/serialize rapid distinct ACPX launches?
rationale: Current code and tests deliberately allow different ACP session keys to run in parallel, so changing that behavior to avoid this failure would be a product and compatibility choice rather than a mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Preserve parallelism, prove launch readiness
options.body: Run a live ACPX/Claude two-spawn reproduction and fix the ACPX/OpenClaw launch-readiness boundary without globally serializing distinct child sessions.

options.title: Gate distinct ACPX launches
options.body: Intentionally serialize or throttle rapid ACPX child launches, then update tests and docs to make the reduced concurrency contract explicit.

options.title: Wait for fresh evidence
options.body: Keep the issue in needs-info until a current ACPX/Claude repro identifies whether the old symptom still exists.

recommendation.title: Preserve parallelism, prove launch readiness
recommendation.body: Run a live ACPX/Claude two-spawn reproduction and fix the ACPX/OpenClaw launch-readiness boundary without globally serializing distinct child sessions.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent ACPX embedding and runtime-surface work make this the best available routing owner for the launch-readiness versus concurrency tradeoff.
